params.comment: projects_dir: where Claude Code keeps session transcripts; a ~/ path is under home, an absolute one is itself, any other is under the repo root. project_match (default the repo's own project folder) names no path here. entrypoint: the transcript value that marks a desktop app session; a terminal session is not this tab's. usage_sessions: N, the docs' own window for Not used recently. app_servers: servers the desktop app adds itself, which its connector list does not show and a user cannot switch off as connectors; an entry ending in _ is a prefix, any other a whole name. human_origin: the origin kind of a record a person typed. plan_tool, recap_tool, session_tool and archive_tool: the app's tools for the task list, the closing recap, starting a session and archiving one. session_id_pattern: how a started session's id reads in the tool's result. idle_hours: a session whose last record is newer may still be running, so its open last turn and unarchived sub-sessions are left out; it is no measuring window. kept_kinds: kinds of server (plugin servers, account connectors, other servers) a repo's owner keeps on for other work; they are set aside from desktop_app.connectors_unused and still count in desktop_app.listing_tokens. None by default.

label: Connectors that fail or need sign-in
means: Servers the session lists that failed to connect or still wait for a sign-in, so they give no tools.
goal_source: goal from the MCP docs: a server that needs authentication or failed to connect gives no tools until it is fixed (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp, read 2026-11-10), and the best practices say to turn off the servers not needed (code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices, read 2026-11-10), so none stays broken
source: state: the newest transcript of this repo whose entrypoint is params.entrypoint, its last deferred_tools_delta attachment: needsAuthMcpServers plus failedMcpServers, counted; the attachment is observed in transcripts, not named in Anthropic's public docs

label: Plugins loaded and not used
means: Plugins whose skills, agents and servers load into every session though no recent session called one.
goal_source: goal from the plugin docs: an enabled plugin is part of every session, and Not used recently means unused for 10 sessions and 14 days (code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/measure, read 2026-11-10); the session count is held here, a calendar window is not
source: state: the plugins named in the newest desktop session's skill listing, agent listing and server lists (the name before the colon, or after plugin_ in a tool name), against Skill, Agent and server calls in the last params.usage_sessions desktop sessions with their subagents; N = 10 sessions, the docs' own window

label: Connectors loaded and not used
means: Connected servers whose tool names and instructions load every session though no recent session called one.
goal_source: goal from the best practices: connected servers add their tool names and instructions even when unused, so turn off the ones not needed (code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices and code.claude.com/docs/en/costs, read 2026-11-10)
source: state: the servers behind the mcp__ tool names the newest desktop session lists, those in params.app_servers and of a kind in params.kept_kinds set aside, against calls in the last params.usage_sessions desktop sessions with their subagents; N = 10 sessions, the window of desktop_app.plugins_unused

label: Work turns with a task list and a recap
means: Turns that changed files or ran commands, kept the task list a person follows, and ended with a recap.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: the task list and the closing recap are how a person follows a session without reading it, so nearly every work turn has both
source: the last params.turn_count work turns a person started in this repo's desktop sessions (a user record whose origin is params.human_origin, then an edit or two or more commands): the share with a params.plan_tool call and a params.recap_tool call; a turn that ends on a question, a plan approval or an interrupt is left out, and so is the open last turn of a session active within params.idle_hours; N = 20 turns, so a day's work replaces it

label: Sub-sessions closed by their starter
means: Sessions that a session started for a task and later archived, so none is left running or forgotten.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: a session that starts another owns it to the end, and the desktop docs archive a session once its work is done (code.claude.com/docs/en/desktop, Archive a session, read 2026-11-10)
source: the last params.sub_session_count sessions started with params.session_tool in this repo's desktop sessions: the share whose id the starting session later passed to params.archive_tool; one not yet archived in a session active within params.idle_hours is left out; N = 10 sub-sessions

label: Subagent runs killed or failed
means: Subagent runs that were stopped or failed before returning a result; their tokens bought nothing.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: a stopped run returns nothing for the tokens it used, so it stays rare
source: the last params.notice_count task notifications that answer a params.agent_tool call in this repo's desktop sessions: the share whose status is in params.bad_statuses; N = 50 notifications

label: Connectors still connecting at the first prompt
means: Servers not yet connected when the session takes its first prompt; their tools cannot be called until they are.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: every tool a session lists is ready when its work begins
source: state: pendingMcpServers of the newest desktop session's first deferred_tools_delta attachment, those in params.app_servers set aside, counted

label: Agent calls sent together
means: Subagents started in one message with the others of their turn, not in the next with nothing learned between.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: the sub-agents docs run independent work in parallel (code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, read 2026-11-10) and give no number
source: the last params.agent_turn_count turns with two or more params.agent_tool calls in this repo's desktop sessions: of those calls, the share not sent in a later message than the turn's previous one with no tool result, notice or message between; a call sent after one of those is taken to depend on it, and the result of an agent that only launched (params.async_status) is none of them; N = 20 turns

label: Listing tokens a session loads
means: Names and descriptions of every skill, agent, server and tool, which each session carries whether it uses them or not.
goal_source: goal from the skills docs: the skill listing budget is 1% of the model's context window (code.claude.com/docs/en/skills, Skill descriptions are cut short, read 2026-11-10), at a 1,000,000-token window = 10,000 tokens, held here for all four listings together; near at 2%, the docs' example of a raised budget
source: state: bytes / 4 of the newest desktop session's skill_listing content, agent_listing_delta lines, mcp_instructions_delta blocks and deferred_tools_delta lines, every delta of the session added up

label: Context the heaviest subagent type starts with
means: What a subagent carries into its first model call, for the agent type that carries most; every run pays it again.
goal_source: template goal, no public benchmark: a subagent inherits every tool unless its definition lists them (code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, read 2026-11-10), so one given only what its task needs starts small
source: the last params.subagent_runs subagent transcripts of this repo's desktop sessions: input plus cache-write plus cache-read tokens of each run's first model call (message.usage), the median of each agent type, the largest; rows from Claude Code 2.1.307 on; N = 20 runs
